entries.title: A Short Walk Can Change Your Day
entries.titleZh: 一次短途步行也能改变一天

difficulty.label: 基础
difficulty.reason: 高频动词和短句为主，因果关系直接。

entries.body: Many people think exercise only counts when it is long, difficult, or done in a gym. That idea can make movement feel like another task on a busy list. In fact, even one session of moderate activity can offer immediate benefits. A brisk walk may help you feel less anxious, sleep better, and lower your blood pressure for a time. Regular movement adds longer-term benefits, including stronger bones and a lower risk of several chronic diseases. The useful lesson is not to wait for a perfect workout. You can walk during a phone call, take the stairs, or get off the bus one stop early. Start with a small action that fits your real day. When it becomes easy, add a few more minutes. A short walk will not solve every health problem, but it can be a realistic first step. Consistency grows more easily from a simple habit than from an ambitious plan you cannot repeat.
entries.guideZh: 今天从一个很实际的问题开始：运动必须很累、很久才算数吗？先听文章，抓住作者如何用“即时收益”和“长期收益”改变这个常见看法。

entries.title: Waste Less Food, One Shelf at a Time
entries.titleZh: 从一层冰箱开始减少食物浪费

difficulty.label: 基础
difficulty.reason: 生活场景具体，动作词丰富，信息结构清晰。

entries.body: Food waste often begins with good intentions. We buy fresh vegetables for several meals, forget what is already in the refrigerator, and then discover spoiled food at the end of the week. A simple system can prevent much of this waste. Before shopping, look through the refrigerator, freezer, and pantry. Plan a few meals around food that needs to be used soon, then write a list with realistic quantities. At home, place older food where you can see it and label leftovers with a date. The freezer is also useful for bread, fruit, and cooked meals that you will not eat in time. These habits save more than food. They also save the water, land, energy, and work used to produce and transport it. The goal is not a perfectly organized kitchen. It is a kitchen that gives you clear signals about what to eat next. One visible shelf and one weekly list are enough to begin.
entries.guideZh: 这篇文章讨论一个很日常的系统设计问题：怎样让厨房主动提醒我们先吃什么。听的时候留意购物前、储存时和吃不完时的三个动作。

entries.title: Coral: An Animal with a Plant Partner
entries.titleZh: 珊瑚：与植物伙伴共生的动物

difficulty.label: 进阶
difficulty.reason: 包含生物学概念、关系从句和过程描述。

entries.body: Coral may look like a colorful underwater plant, but it is an animal. A coral colony is built by hundreds or thousands of tiny creatures called polyps. Each polyp attaches to a surface and uses small tentacles to collect food from the water. Many reef-building corals also live in partnership with microscopic algae inside their tissues. The algae use sunlight to make food. In return for protection and access to the coral's waste products, they provide oxygen and nutrients that help the coral grow. This partnership is called symbiosis. When water becomes too warm or other conditions create stress, coral may push the algae out. Without its colorful partner, the coral turns white, a process known as bleaching. A bleached coral is not necessarily dead, but it has lost an important source of energy and is more vulnerable. Understanding this relationship explains both the remarkable strength of a reef and its sensitivity to environmental change.

entries.title: Why the Moon Comes Before Mars
entries.titleZh: 为什么先去月球，再去火星

difficulty.label: 进阶
difficulty.reason: 包含目的表达、技术词汇和多层因果关系。

entries.body: Mars is a long-term goal for human exploration, but the Moon offers a more practical place to prepare. A crew can reach the Moon in days, while a round trip to Mars could take years. That difference matters when engineers test life-support systems, landing technology, and ways to use local resources. If equipment fails near the Moon, teams can study the problem and bring lessons home much faster. The lunar surface also keeps a record of events that shaped the early solar system. Studying its rocks may help scientists understand the history of both the Moon and Earth. NASA's Artemis program combines these scientific questions with a larger engineering challenge: learning how people and robots can work together far from Earth for longer periods. The Moon is therefore not simply a final destination. It is a nearby laboratory where explorers can test ideas under real conditions. Each successful test reduces uncertainty before crews attempt the much longer and more demanding journey to Mars.
entries.guideZh: 今天的问题不是“月球还是火星”，而是为什么探索需要分阶段。听文章时抓住距离、风险、科学价值三个理由。

entries.title: Four Verbs for More Trustworthy AI
entries.titleZh: 可信 AI 的四个行动词

difficulty.label: 高阶
difficulty.reason: 抽象概念密集，包含框架语言、权衡与组织治理表达。

entries.body: Artificial intelligence can create value, but it can also affect people in ways that are difficult to predict. A useful risk process must therefore continue throughout an AI system's life, rather than appear as a final checklist. The NIST AI Risk Management Framework organizes this work around four verbs: govern, map, measure, and manage. To govern is to define responsibility, policies, and a culture that takes risk seriously. To map is to understand the system's purpose, users, context, and possible impacts. To measure is to test performance and examine evidence about qualities such as safety, privacy, fairness, and reliability. To manage is to prioritize the risks that have been found, choose responses, and monitor what happens after deployment. These actions influence one another. Better context improves measurement, while new evidence may change management decisions or governance rules. The framework does not promise that every trade-off will disappear. Instead, it gives teams a shared language for asking better questions, documenting choices, and revisiting them as technology and real-world conditions change.
entries.guideZh: 把这篇文章看成一份框架导读。四个动词不是线性的清单，而是一套持续循环的风险管理语言。
entries.keyIdeaZh: 可信 AI 不是一次验收的结果，而是贯穿系统生命周期的持续治理过程。

entries.title: Why We Always See the Same Side of the Moon
entries.titleZh: 为什么我们总看到月球的同一面

difficulty.label: 进阶
difficulty.reason: 包含复合句、过程解释和适量学科词汇，逻辑关系明确。

entries.body: The Moon travels around Earth while also turning slowly on its own axis. One lunar rotation takes almost the same amount of time as one orbit around our planet. Because these two motions stay synchronized, the same lunar hemisphere usually faces Earth. The far side is not permanently dark; it receives sunlight during every lunar month. Changing sunlight creates the phases we see, from a thin crescent to a full Moon. Impact craters, cooled lava, and ancient ice make the lunar surface a record of solar-system history. Synchronized motion explains our familiar view without implying that the Moon has stopped rotating. Understanding this relationship turns an everyday sight into a clear lesson about motion and perspective. Careful comparison helps readers separate an exciting image from the physical process and evidence that explain it.
entries.guideZh: 听文章时区分 rotation、orbit 和 phase，理解两个周期同步后产生的视觉结果。

entries.title: A Day on Mars Feels Familiar, but a Year Does Not
entries.titleZh: 火星的一天很熟悉，一年却很不同

difficulty.label: 进阶
difficulty.reason: 包含复合句、过程解释和适量学科词汇，逻辑关系明确。

entries.body: Mars completes one rotation in about 24.6 hours, so a Martian day is close to an Earth day. Scientists call that day a sol, a useful word when they plan rover operations. A Martian year is much longer because Mars follows a wider path around the Sun. It takes about 687 Earth days for Mars to complete a single orbit. Mars also has seasons because its axis is tilted in a way that resembles Earth. However, its elliptical orbit makes those seasons unequal in length and more extreme in some regions. A familiar daily rhythm can therefore exist inside a calendar that feels completely different. Mission teams must translate between sols and Earth dates when they schedule science and communicate results. Careful comparison helps readers separate an exciting image from the physical process and evidence that explain it.

entries.body: From space, Earth looks blue because oceans cover most of its surface. Liquid water is only one part of the system that makes our planet unusual. The atmosphere contains gases that support life and help regulate surface temperature. A magnetic field also deflects many charged particles arriving from the Sun. Land, ocean, air, ice, and living things constantly exchange energy and material. A change in one part of this connected system can influence many other parts. Earth stays habitable through relationships among water, air, rock, sunlight, and life. Seeing the planet as a system helps scientists study both local events and global change. Careful comparison helps readers separate an exciting image from the physical process and evidence that explain it.

entries.title: The Sun Holds the Solar System Together

entries.body: The Sun is an ordinary star in one sense, yet it dominates our local neighborhood in space. Its gravity keeps planets, dwarf planets, asteroids, and comets moving in stable paths. Deep inside the Sun, nuclear fusion combines hydrogen and releases enormous amounts of energy. That energy takes time to travel outward before reaching Earth as light and heat. Sunlight powers photosynthesis, influences weather, and supports almost every food chain on our planet. Solar activity can also disturb satellites, radio communication, navigation, and electrical systems. The Sun is both a steady source of life-giving energy and a changing space-weather environment. Studying it helps scientists understand stars while protecting technology used in daily life. Careful comparison helps readers separate an exciting image from the physical process and evidence that explain it.

entries.body: Venus is similar to Earth in size, but its surface conditions are dramatically different. A thick atmosphere made mostly of carbon dioxide traps heat with an intense greenhouse effect. Surface temperatures are high enough to melt lead, even though Venus is not the closest planet to the Sun. Clouds of sulfuric acid hide the surface from ordinary visible-light cameras. Radar instruments can look through those clouds and map mountains, plains, and volcanic features. Venus rotates very slowly and in the opposite direction from most planets. Similar size does not guarantee a similar climate when atmospheric history develops differently. By studying Venus, scientists test ideas about climate, geology, and the evolution of rocky worlds. Careful comparison helps readers separate an exciting image from the physical process and evidence that explain it.

entries.body: Saturn is famous for rings that can be seen even with a modest telescope. The rings contain countless pieces of ice and rock, ranging from dust-sized grains to much larger chunks. They appear solid from far away, but wide gaps separate many of their particles. Gravity from Saturn and its moons shapes ring edges, waves, and narrow divisions. Some material falls gradually into the planet, while collisions continue to change the ring system. Scientists therefore do not expect the rings to remain exactly as they are forever. A beautiful structure can look permanent on a human timescale while still evolving astronomically. Saturn offers a visible laboratory for studying gravity, collisions, and change across a planetary system. Careful comparison helps readers separate an exciting image from the physical process and evidence that explain it.

entries.title: Asteroids Preserve an Ancient Record
entries.titleZh: 小行星保存着远古记录

difficulty.label: 高阶
difficulty.reason: 信息密度较高，包含抽象概念、限定表达和专业词汇。

entries.body: Asteroids are rocky remnants left from the formation of the solar system about 4.6 billion years ago. Most orbit the Sun between Mars and Jupiter, but others follow paths that approach Earth. Their shapes are often irregular because many are too small for gravity to make them round. Some asteroids are loose collections of material held together weakly by gravity. Spacecraft can measure their composition, photograph their surfaces, and sometimes return samples to Earth. Those samples preserve chemical clues that have been altered or erased on active planets. A small object can carry evidence about conditions that existed before Earth fully formed.
